statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-50195 (GO-2026-5338, GHSA-cvxm-645q-p574): containerd's CRI checkpoint import did not validate the image references in a checkpoint image's configuration, so a user who can create pods can make containerd pull an attacker's image and give it an arbitrary local tag, poisoning the node's image cache. It is fixed in containerd 2.3.2, 2.2.5 and 2.1.9 by a change to checkpoint restore in containerd's internal/cri/server package (https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-cvxm-645q-p574, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5338, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.3.2, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.2.5). Read the Go build information and the function table (with a reader of the Go symbol table that also works on stripped binaries) of every Go program in every build-dev package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 89 builds, 2.6.4-r0 through the current 2.29.1-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only, every download checked against the index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index; the copy the repository serves, which matches one of those entries' checksum, was read. Each package holds one file, the frontend Go program /usr/bin/build. runtime.main is found in the function table of every Go program scanned, so the tables were read. The build information of the frontend program lists github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 v2.2.0 through v2.3.7 across the builds, but the vulnerable code is not linked in. In every build, the only containerd packages in its function table are core/remotes/docker, core/remotes/docker/auth, core/remotes/errors, internal/lazyregexp, pkg/identifiers, pkg/reference and version (all under github.com/containerd/containerd/v2), and no function table of any Go program in any build contains a function from containerd's internal/cri/server package. As a positive control, the same reader lists internal/cri/server functions, including github.com/containerd/containerd/v2/internal/cri/server.(*criService).CheckpointContainer, in /usr/bin/containerd from the DHI containerd 2.4.2-r5 package. The vulnerable code is not present in this package, so the containerd version recorded in its build information does not make it affected.

CVE-2026-50195: containerd's CRI checkpoint import does not validate the image references in a checkpoint image's configuration, so a user who can create pods can make containerd pull an image and give it an arbitrary local tag. The vulnerable code is containerd's CRI server, github.com/containerd/containerd/v2/internal/cri/server, in criService.CRImportCheckpoint and criService.CreateContainer, which the Go vulnerability database lists as the affected symbols; it is fixed in containerd 2.1.9, 2.2.5 and 2.3.2: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-cvxm-645q-p574 and https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5338. The fix commit the Go database lists, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/0c0918fa8fb4d997f889a3d811603995a3a2b68a (main branch, cri: do not re-tag restored checkpoints), changes only internal/cri/server/container_checkpoint_linux.go and a test script. We read every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each package checked against the index checksum. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 that keeps its Go symbol table. Its Go build information lists github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 v2.2.0 to v2.3.7, with no replace directive; builds 0.69.1-r0 to 0.70.0-r6 also list the older github.com/containerd/containerd module (1.7.29 to 1.7.32), which this advisory does not cover. trivy links containerd's client, content, images and remotes packages, and through them four of containerd's internal helper packages (internal/cleanup, internal/kmutex, internal/lazyregexp and internal/randutil), but the function table of every build has no function from containerd's CRI packages (internal/cri, pkg/cri or plugins/cri) and no criService method, while runtime.main is found in each build. A byte search of every build also finds no internal/cri, cri/server, criService or CRImportCheckpoint string, while github.com/containerd/containerd/v2/client. is found in each. As a positive control, we built containerd's own cmd/containerd from the vulnerable v2.3.1 tag for amd64 and arm64: the same function-table read finds 1271 CRI functions there, including internal/cri/server.(*criService).CRImportCheckpoint and (*criService).CreateContainer, and the same byte search finds CRImportCheckpoint 13 times. The vulnerable CRI code is not in the shipped binary.
